mission: Elya finds a duplicated wartime quarantine/survey shipment manifest from the final days before the Battle of Shedu Maad. One version is public and boring; the hidden duplicate carries the same shipment identity, a quarantine/survey disguise, conflicting destination data, and enough metadata to show Jacen Solo personally encrypted it shortly before his death. She realizes this is not a clerical duplicate: one of Jacen’s last orders had two lives. She remembers the old wrong approval field where she once quietly removed Ben’s name because he had been fourteen and she could not bear one more child being turned into a clean bureaucratic answer. She sends Ben the obsolete GAG-coded message through an identity-address/dead-drop protocol tied to his old service marker: GAG is still active. One of Jacen’s last orders has two lives. Come alone. — E.R. Then she hears someone arrive. Aevyn reaches her. He uses a Jacen-derived form of weaponized Recognition to extract part of the lead. The method is precise, intimate, and controlled rather than showy. He learns that Elya contacted Ben, preserved a missing piece, and found a Jacen-sealed duplicate manifest pointing toward Iresh. He pushes the mind and body past what they can survive. Elya dies — but the damaged manifest fragment she preserved remains beyond what Aevyn fully extracts.
why_now: Elya has spent days staring at a routine records anomaly that turned into something she cannot unsee: Jacen Solo personally encrypted a wartime duplicate manifest days before his death, and the hidden copy went somewhere the public shipment never did. She has to send the warning tonight, while she still can.
conflict: Elya wants to get her warning to Ben and preserve the fragment before whoever sealed this record notices she has found it. Her obstacle is that the office is a dead end — no exits she can reach in time — and Aevyn arrives before she is gone. He wants to extract what she knows and where she sent it, and he has a method she has no defense against.
setting: Coruscant, late night, third-floor records office of the Coruscant Bureau of Post-Conflict Logistics — a narrow internal office with six workstations and no windows. Five desks are dark; only Elya's terminal is lit. The chrono on the wall reads 0233 when the scene opens, 0300 when it closes. Climate-control hum, terminal hum, recycled-air feel. After Aevyn enters: claustrophobic; no escape route Elya can reach in time.
emotional_trajectory: Elya should be competent, afraid, and briefly human before the plot kills her. The reader should feel that a decent person is being erased, not merely that an inciting incident has occurred. Aevyn should be frightening before he is explained — avoid sympathy or backstory here; make the reader feel the wrongness of his method.

stakes.personal: Elya fears that the system she survived is still alive and that she helped keep it alive by doing nothing earlier. She wants one old choice — moving Ben's name out of the wrong approval field — to matter one more time.
stakes.interpersonal: Aevyn has all the power and a method Elya has no counter to. The scene's dynamic is precise predator versus trapped bureaucrat: she is trying to hide what she sent and where, he is systematically taking it from her.
stakes.external: If Aevyn recovers everything Elya knows, the investigation dies here. The fragment she hid by records instinct — not in an obvious safe — is the only piece he cannot fully extract. That gap is what keeps the mystery alive after she is gone.

sensory_details: The climate-control hum and the fluorescent buzz of the single lit terminal at 0233 — everything else dark and silent. The recycled air tastes of old plasticrete and heat-stressed electronics. When Aevyn enters, Elya notices the absence of sound first: no footsteps, just the door-seal click and suddenly a man standing between her and the corridor.
canon_elements_needed: Shedu Maad / Hapes Jedi HQ continuity
Iresh physical geography and local survival rules

turning_point_detail.trigger: Aevyn uses Recognition-derived memory pressure to pull what Elya sent and to whom — he learns Ben's name, the fragment's existence, and that it points toward Iresh. He pushes past what she can survive.
turning_point_detail.shift: Elya dies. But the damaged manifest fragment she hid by records instinct — not in the obvious terminal, not in any field Aevyn could read cleanly — survives beyond his extraction.
turning_point_detail.cost: A decent person is erased. The only witness to what she found is gone. The warning she sent to Ben is now irrevocable — and so is Aevyn's knowledge that Ben received it.

emotional_arc.start: Elya is tense and purposeful — she has already sent the message, she is still telling herself this might be nothing, she is moving fast through the thing you do when fear is in the room but you refuse to name it.
emotional_arc.shift: When Aevyn enters, purposeful tips into controlled terror. She understands immediately that this is not a colleague or a security sweep. She uses every procedural instinct she has — keep talking, keep her hands visible, think in fields not bodies — as a last defense.
emotional_arc.end: Elya dies as herself: practical, tense, and briefly human. The reader should feel the loss of a specific ordinary person, not just an inciting incident.

key_beats.beat_description: Elya sits alone at 0233 with two versions of the same wartime shipment manifest open on her terminal — the public record is routine, the hidden duplicate carries Jacen Solo's personal encryption marker.
key_beats.state_change: Elya confirms the anomaly is not clerical: one of Jacen's last orders had two lives, and she is the only person awake with proof.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The tightening behind the sternum — not panic, the earlier kind; the kind that comes before you decide you have already decided.

key_beats.beat_description: Elya composes and sends the GAG dead-drop message to Ben's old service marker, then hides the manifest fragment in a location her records instinct selects rather than any documented procedure.
key_beats.state_change: The warning is now irrevocable; the fragment is hidden where no one who searches by procedure will look first.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Hands moving on muscle memory, brain slightly behind them — the familiar feeling of making a records correction before anyone can call it a choice.

key_beats.beat_description: The door-seal clicks and Aevyn is standing between Elya and the corridor, having entered without a sound she registered.
key_beats.state_change: The office becomes a closed room; every exit Elya had is now behind him.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The absence of footsteps — she notices that first, and the noticing is worse than a shout would have been.

key_beats.beat_description: Aevyn applies Recognition-derived memory pressure — precise, intimate, and systematic — to extract what Elya sent, to whom, and where the manifest points.
key_beats.state_change: Aevyn learns Ben's name, the fragment's existence, and the Iresh destination; Elya's procedural instincts are her only defense and they are not enough.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The impulse to think in fields instead of bodies — keep it bureaucratic, keep it abstracted, buy one more second by staying in the vocabulary of records and not the vocabulary of dying.

key_beats.beat_description: Elya dies; the fragment she hid by instinct survives in a location Aevyn's extraction does not reach.
key_beats.state_change: The only witness is gone, but the gap in Aevyn's knowledge — the undiscovered fragment — keeps the investigation alive.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Not applicable — Elya's arc ends here; the pov_reaction is the reader's, not hers: the specific wrongness of watching a decent, ordinary person be erased.
